text: This guide shows you how to buy eyeglasses in Germany. It explains what your health insurance pays for, and how to pay less for your glasses.

section: Does public health insurance cover glasses?
text: Usually, no.Public health insurancerarely pays for eyeglasses, but there are some exceptions: Children under 18 years oldInsurance pays for the lenses, but not the frame.1 AdultsInsurance pays for the lenses, but only in those cases:2You are near-sighted (myopia), and your glasses’ strength is over 6 dioptresor you are far-sighted (hyperopia), and your glasses’ strength is over 6 dioptresor you have astigmatism, and your glasses’ strength is over 4 dioptresor the glasses are needed to treat eye injuries or eye diseases, for example to protect your eyes after an eye surgery You are near-sighted (myopia), and your glasses’ strength is over 6 dioptres or you are far-sighted (hyperopia), and your glasses’ strength is over 6 dioptres or you have astigmatism, and your glasses’ strength is over 4 dioptres or the glasses are needed to treat eye injuries or eye diseases, for example to protect your eyes after an eye surgery In those cases, health insurance only pays for basic lenses.3It does not pay for the frame. Some opticians will give you the frame for free, like Fielmann and itsNulltarif collection. When you buy glasses, the optician charges your health insurance directly. You don’t need to ask for a reimbursement.4You must buy eyeglasses less than 4 weeks after getting an eye test.4

section: Does public health insurance cover glasses?
title: Are contact lenses covered?
text: No. The rules for contact lenses are the same as for eyeglasses.

section: Does public health insurance cover glasses?
title: Are eye tests covered?
text: Yes. If you go to an ophthalmologist (Augenarzt), the eye test is free.5Your health insurance pays for it. If you have a prescription, and you need glasses for your work,your employer must pay for them. If you go to an optician (Optiker), the test is not covered by your insurance. You must pay for the test yourself. There is one exception:TKpays for tests at the optician, but only for children under 14 years old.6

section: Does private health insurance cover glasses?
text: Sometimes.Many private health insurers pay for eyeglasses. Usually, you can spend a fixed amount on eyeglasses every 2 or 3 years. Private health insurancecoverage varies a lot. You must check your insurance policy (underHilfsmittel). If you are stillchoosing health insurance,ask my insurance expertto help you find health insurance that covers glasses.

Sometimes. If you need glasses to do your job, your employer must pay for your glasses. Your employer must pay for your glasses if…7 You needcomputer glasses(Bildschirmarbeitsplatzbrille) for your job. For example if you work in front of a screen more than 45 minutes a day. You need a prescription from an ophthalmologist (Augenarzt). You needprotective glassesfor your work. For example, if you work in construction.

Some insurers also offer glasses insurance (Brillenversicherung). It costs around €7per month. Usually, it pays for new glasses every 2 years. Usually,it’s not worth it.8The insurance is more expensive than the glasses it pays for. It rarely cover lost glasses.9

section: How to pay less for eyeglasses
text: A normal pair of eyeglasses costs around €350. This includes the frame and the lenses. There are ways to pay less.

section: How to pay less for eyeglasses
title: Buy generic frames
text: Frames from popular brands cost €150to €350. Generic frames often cost less than €100. You can even find eyeglasses for less than €50, lenses included. These stores sell generic frames: Ace + TateGeneric frames starting at €100. They have3 storesin Berlin. Brillenplatz.de(German)Cheaper glasses with generic frames for less than €50. Fielmann(German)TheNulltarif collectioncosts less than €20. They havehundreds of branchesin Germany. Mister Spex(German)Cheaper glasses with generic frames. They havedozens of branchesin Germany. They also let you try different frames at home, and return the ones you don’t like.10 Robin Look(German)Cheaper glasses with generic frames. They havedozens of branchesin Germany. When you visit an optician, they usually show you expensive frames first. Say that you don’t want to pay a lot, and ask to see the generic options.

section: How to pay less for eyeglasses
title: Get your eye test at the eye doctor
text: If you havepublic health insurance, get tested at the ophthalmologist (Augenarzt). The test is covered by your health insurance. If you go to an optician, you must pay around €25for the test. Usually, the test is free if you also buy eyeglasses. If you take a first aid class for yourdriving licence, it usually includes a free eye test.16

section: How to pay less for eyeglasses
title: Deduct glasses from your taxes
text: You can deduct eyeglasses from your taxes.11If you went to an ophthalmologist (Augenarzt), you can also deduct your eye test.12 You must deduct it as an exceptional burden (außergewöhnliche Belastung).13You must have an eye test from an ophthalmologist (Augenarzt), to prove that you need glasses.14 You can’t deduct glasses as a business expense (Werbungskosten), unless you only use them at work.15For example, if you buy safety goggles for work, you can deduct them as a business expense. aok.de,§ 33 SGB V,bundesgesundheitsministerium.de⤴ aok.de,§ 33 SGB V,bundesgesundheitsministerium.de⤴ patientenberatung.de(2022),§ 33 SGB V⤴ patientenberatung.de(2022),§ 33 SGB V⤴ brille24.de⤴ brille24.de⤴ patientenberatung.de(2022)⤴ patientenberatung.de(2022)⤴ tk.de,brillen-sehhilfen.de,aok.de⤴ tk.de,brillen-sehhilfen.de,aok.de⤴ tk.de⤴ tk.de⤴ gesetze-im-internet.de,blickcheck.de⤴ gesetze-im-internet.de,blickcheck.de⤴ versicherungsmonitor.de⤴ versicherungsmonitor.de⤴ verti.de⤴ verti.de⤴ misterspex.de⤴ misterspex.de⤴ taxfix.de,vlh.de⤴ taxfix.de,vlh.de⤴ kann-man-das-absetzen.de⤴ kann-man-das-absetzen.de⤴ taxfix.de⤴ taxfix.de⤴ gesetze-im-internet.de,taxfix.de,taxfix.de⤴ gesetze-im-internet.de,taxfix.de,taxfix.de⤴ vlh.de⤴ vlh.de⤴ ArbeitNow(2025)⤴ ArbeitNow(2025)⤴
